definitions.explanation: A piece of hard candy or boiled sweet. From English 'candy.' In Japanese, this word typically refers to hard candies specifically, as opposed to chocolate or other confections.

examples.japanese: キャンディー⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧なめる。
のど⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{痛|いた}い→痛い：01108_itai⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で、キャンディー⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{買|か}った→買う：00489_kau⟧。
examples.english: I bought some candy because my throat hurts.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}どもたち⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦カラフル→カラフル：10803_karafuru⟧なキャンディー⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{配|くば}ったら→配る：03921_kubaru⟧、⟦みんな→みんな：02972_minna⟧⟦{喜|よろこ}んだ→喜ぶ：01169_yorokobu⟧。
examples.english: When I handed out colorful candies to the children, they were all delighted.

notes:
A loanword from English 'candy.' In Japanese, キャンディー generally refers to hard candies or boiled sweets, while broader categories of sweets have different terms. The shorter form キャンディ is also used.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- キャンディー⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧なめる: to suck on a candy
- キャンディー⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{配|くば}る→配る：03921_kubaru⟧: to hand out candy
- ⟦フルーツ→フルーツ：11247_furuutsu⟧キャンディー: fruit candy
- のどキャンディー: throat candy; cough drop

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{飴|あめ}→飴：00687_ame⟧: candy; hard candy — the native Japanese word, more commonly used in everyday speech
- ⟦お{菓子|かし}→お菓子：02852_okashi⟧: sweets; snacks — broader term covering all confections
- ドロップ: drop candy — hard candy, often fruit-flavored, in a tin
- ⟦チョコレート→チョコレート：05183_chokoreeto⟧: chocolate — a different category of confection
